Trust signals are rendered only when present, so an unverified technician shows a near-blank card — the absence of Aadhaar or police verification, the single most important safety datum, is communicated by nothing at all rather than by an explicit 'not verified' state.
Ratings are drawn as repeated '★' text characters with no numeric value and no aria-label, making the rating inaccessible to screen readers and unreadable if the glyph is missing.
The loading affordance is a hardcoded English 'Loading…' in gray-400 on gray-50 (~2.6:1), failing AA, while the app already ships a .skeleton shimmer.
The error message interpolates a raw HTTP status code into an English sentence and offers no retry.
Review dates are produced by slicing the raw ISO timestamp to 10 characters instead of using formatDateTime, so this is the only date in the admin rendered in ISO rather than locale form.
The whole dossier renders at 12px with six hardcoded Tailwind gray values on a gray-50 card inside a white slide-over — three layers of off-token light-mode styling inside a dark-default admin.
The disclosure uses a bare '▾'/'▸' text glyph with no aria-hidden and no aria-controls, so the triangle character is announced and the region is not programmatically associated.
Certifications and languages are rendered as raw comma-joined strings rather than chips, inconsistent with the verification badges directly above them that do use .chip-success.
The dossier fetch calls apiUrl directly with no credentials option, unlike AuditLogClient which sets credentials: 'include'.

Filters are wired directly into a useCallback dependency that a useEffect depends on, so every keystroke in any of the six filter fields triggers a fresh network request and a full table unmount — no debounce, no submit.
Two error paths produce inconsistent messages: a non-ok HTTP response yields the hardcoded English 'API error: {status}' while a thrown exception yields the translated loadFailed string.

Pagination is continuation-token only — there is no total count, no page number, no jump-to-page, and no result count anywhere on the screen, so an operator cannot tell how much audit history a filter matched.
The loading indicator is a plain sentence with no role=status, so the disappearance of the table is the only loading signal for a screen-reader operator.

handlePrevPage pops the stack and refetches with the new top token, but on the first back-step it passes undefined, meaning 'previous' from page 2 refetches page 1 correctly while deeper history relies on a stack that is also reset by any filter change (line 52).
There is no export affordance on the audit log, unlike the orders console which has CSV export — a compliance record that cannot be exported.
